headline: Benchmarks against truth sets are defining somatic and structural variant detection
label: Somatic Variant Benchmarking Methods
summary: SMaHT and multi-institution studies release shared cell-line mixtures and synthetic resources to test low-allele-fraction somatic calling across platforms.
synthesis: The dominant thread is benchmarking variant detection against defined truth. The SMaHT Network benchmarks sequencing technologies and somatic mutation callers, releasing multi-platform datasets that span bulk and single-cell sequencing. A multi-institution study uses a 1:49 cell-line mixture with ultra-deep short- and long-read WGS across five centers to test low-VAF SNV and indel calling. A pangenome-graph method constructs a synthetic somatic resource from six HapMap mixtures, covering SNVs, indels, SVs and MEIs at 0.25%–16.5% VAF. Related structural variant work benchmarks 16 short-read callers and ensemble pipelines against HG002 truth sets, finding that ensembles often reduce breakpoint accuracy. The newest element is the emphasis on shared reference resources and cross-platform evaluation rather than performance of individual callers.
